body: `is_backup_save_enabled` can be removed entirely, it was only used in `FileAccess` implementation and not exposed.

New method (and corresponding constants) should be probably exposed to scripting in `FileAccess::_bind_methods()`.

Also, `_open` wrapper used for scripting should be updated (and have compatibility method added) to have a new `SaveIntegrityLevel p_integrity_level` argument.

Also when adding this binding, you will also want to expose the `SaveIntegrityLevel` enum. The documentation on the enum can then be moved out of the code comments into the class reference .xml files.


I see you're adding `const` to some `int` parameters but not to others. My take is the same as always, especially for parameters, it makes readability worse. In any case, if there was consensus to use `const` everywhere it fits, let's do a whole-codebase pass. I'd therefore suggest not adding them in this PR.

Nooo!!!!

This is a left-over from a previous, scrapped idea. Well spotted! Removing this as well.

The only reason I'm using `int` instead of `FileAccess::SaveIntegrityLevel` is to avoid another `#include` as I need to bring file_access.h in. I've seen that pattern in other parts of the API, but used inconsistently.

Personally, I prefer strong type safety; and the fact that header inclusion is exploding throughout the database should be addressed separately(\*).

I can easily change it to `FileAccess::SaveIntegrityLevel`.
Thoughts?


(\*) Something needs to be done about that. A single header is changed and between 25-75% of the project needs to be built again. It's really bad for productivity.

For unexposed `ResourceFormatSaver` it's OK as is.

But I would change it for public `Image` methods, some parts of the code avoid includes from other parts of the complex dependencies, but both `Image` and `FileAccess` are part `core/io`, so adding extra include should be fine.

`ResourceFormatSaver` is part of `core/io` too, so if that's the criteria we can add the header there too.

On the other hand, ResourceFormatSaver is also included in a lot of other modules headers, while file_access.h isn't.
I stand corrected. Image is included in a lot of other module headers too. It makes sense for `ResourceFormatSaver` to also become typed.
There are also `save_encrypted()` and `save_encrypted_pass()`.

what is going on here? `_save_compat_100447` [only takes a `path` argument](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100447/files#diff-3b9dd8590c4e9192c964dc726efa3f1a3911d6956a7902fa19e90453f8cef9edR52) but i see 4 arguments here, including a non reference or pointer `err` argument.
How does this work?

You were looking at `ConfigFile::_save_compat_100447`; but you should be looking at `ResourceFormatSaver::_save_compat_100447` which takes a `path` argument and a `flags` argument. 2 arguments in total.

There are other issues with `ResourceFormatSaver::_save_compat_100447`, I'll be pushing a fix in 10 or 20 minutes.
OK all issues I could find are fixed. CI is till running though.
Done.

I'm willing to accept either way.

My reason for preferring `FileAccess::SAVE_INTEGRITY_DEFAULT` is that it makes it easier to copy paste: any API user will write `foo._open( ... )` and wants to override the default, will see `SaveIntegrityLevel p_integrity_level = SAVE_INTEGRITY_DEFAULT`.

Copy paste SAVE_INTEGRITY_DEFAULT, then:

1. Compiler error.
2. Autocomplete doesn't work either, because `SAVE_INTEGRITY_` does not resolve either.
3. Once the user realizes what's happening, he needs to go to file_access.h, hit Go To Definition on `SAVE_INTEGRITY_DEFAULT` then scroll to the top and see it belongs to `FileAccess`. Aha! Write `FileAccess::`

This is solved by placing the member on the declaration.

Copy pasting `FileAccess::SAVE_INTEGRITY_DEFAULT` works out of the box every time, and `FileAccess::SAVE_INTEGRITY_` works with autocomplete. The quality of life for other C++ users who consume the API is much improved.
That's fair, it's just unusual

I was just following declaration order (since `FileAccess::_open*` family of functions have been and used to be declared before the `store_*` ones).
